The original version of this spec proposed an image property and flavor extra
spec to allow users to opt-in to live migration at the cost of exposing their
Barbican secret to the Nova service user. The intent was to provide a way to
enable live migration for all vTPM instances without requiring operator
intervention. However, this approach was deemed too risky due to the potential
for security implications. As a result, the design has been updated to remove
the image property and flavor extra spec, and instead rely solely on the
instance metadata to determine whether live migration should be allowed.

The ``vtpm_secret_security`` field will be added to the ``instance_system_metadata`` table,
and will be populated during the migration process. The field will be nullable,
as some instances may not have a vTPM secret security policy set.

then perform any kind of instance operation that goes through the
`_create_guest() <https://opendev.org/openstack/nova/src/commit/c79bec0f2257967da1dcccc9f562253d6ede535d/nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py#L8038-L8063>`_

and operators have a legitimate need to perform certain actions on vTPM instances

and assumes libvirt will copy the vTPM state during the live migration.

For vTPM live migration to work, the vTPM secret needs to be defined on the
source and destination hosts so that libvirt can decrypt the vTPM state.
To define it, Nova would need to retrieve it from Barbican. A live migration
is an admin operation, so Nova would attempt the retrieval with either admin's
token, or Nova's service token. Since the vTPM secret is owned by the user
and is not readable by anyone else, such a retrieval would be forbidden.

For privacy and transparency reasons, granting access to the vTPM secret to
the Nova service user for the purposes of live migration should be something
the user does with full knowledge and consent. It cannot be something done by
Nova silently. This spec proposes a flavor extra spec and image property -
